text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Qatari delegation visits Jordan to discuss economic cooperation.
- National Constitutional Party, a merger of nine minor political parties, launched with pledge to protect democracy.
- Interior Minister Nazir Rasheed says government has no current plans to issue a union law but calls on professional unions to get their affairs in order.
- Development is the most important factor in cementing peace, King Hussein says after talks in the Netherlands.
- Jordan to receive in December first batch of F-16 fighter-bombers from the United States. Joint Jordan-U.S. exercises end.
- Unions to discuss today resignation of four union chiefs in protest at new press law.
- King Hussein and French President Jacques Chirac to meet today to discuss Middle East peace process.
- Weekly newspaper Abed-Rebbo to be the first victim of press law; expected to close next week.

- Deputy Prime Minister Jawad al-Anani says Jordan will play an active part in Doha economic summit, if it is held. Amman helping Qatar with preparations and working on projects to present to the summit.
- Aid to Jordan expected to be agreed during Crown Prince Hassan's trip to Washington.
- Sudanese envoys request Jordan's backing for new peace agreement.
